title: Model fleet affinity + KV pressure scenarios (Q1 2026)
summary: This working sheet explores how introducing 2 new medium-sized LLMs plus one experimental large LLM across multiple regions affects GPU pool utilization and KV cache pressure. We use an "affinity"-based customer routing assumption (sticky region/model affinity) and run three probabilistic onboarding schedules to estimate peak KV footprint and steady-state pressure.
context_and_goals: Background: PMs plan to onboard 'Muse-13B' (opt-13b like), 'Breeze-7B' (compact), and trial 'Atlas-70B' in limited regions. Ops needs per-region GPU headroom and persistent KV cache sizing guidance before scheduled canary rollouts.
Primary goal: produce conservative KV and GPU utilization projections by region for planning reserved capacity and cache cluster sizing (Redis/Tiered-KV).
Secondary goal: identify simple mitigation knobs (shorter TTLs, regional pinning, burst-only variants) and quantify potential unit-cost savings.
Audience: infra leads, SRE, release manager, product-engineering onboarding owners.
assumptions: Traffic mix: baseline traffic from hosted customers maps to current fleet usage (baseline Q4 2025 telemetry used).
Affinity routing: 70% of requests remain in original region due to geo-affinity and pinned deployments; 30% cross-region spillover handled by fallback pools.

Model footprints (approx): Breeze-7B: 12GB KV per 1M active prefixes; Muse-13B: 28GB KV per 1M active prefixes; Atlas-70B: 120GB KV per 1M active prefixes (large KV due to wider context + multihead states).
Average request context length distribution: 60% short (<512 tokens), 30% mid (512-2048), 10% long (>2048).
KV representation: we conservatively assume 48 bytes per token of KV state (keys+values+overhead) after quantization and compression in runtime cache layer.
Co-location: Dedicated GPU pools may host multiple models; we account for co-tenancy memory overhead of ~6% per extra model instance on the same node.
TTL policy baseline: 24 hours for pinned prefixes, 1 hour for ephemeral prefixes; we'll model alternate TTLs in scenarios.
scenarios_overview: Scenario A (staggered onboarding): Breeze-7B -> Muse-13B -> Atlas-70B, each onboarded across 2 regions per week (conservative rollout).
Scenario B (burst onboarding): All three models roll into primary regions within a 10-day window to simulate aggressive product launch.
Scenario C (canary-first Atlas): Atlas onboards to a single region first while the two smaller models onboard globally; used to stress-test large-kv behavior early.

For each scenario we estimate: 1) Peak concurrent KV footprint per region (GB), 2) Expected sustained GPU utilization uplift (%), 3) Hot-prefix percentage and required cache hit target to keep latency SLOs.
calculation_examples: Example calc (Muse-13B baseline per-region active prefixes): assume 150k active prefixes in eu-central1 during launch week. Muse-13B KV = (150k / 1,000,000) * 28GB = 4.2GB. Using 48 bytes/token estimate with average stored tokens ~600 per prefix gives rough cross-check: 150k * 600 * 48B = 4.32GB => consistent.

Combined model peak calc (Scenario B, us-west1): Breeze(200k) + Muse(180k) + Atlas(25k) active prefixes => Breeze KV = 2.4GB, Muse KV = 5.04GB, Atlas KV = 3.0GB => total ~10.44GB persistent KV. Add 12% overhead for cache metadata/replication => ~11.7GB.

GPU utilization uplift heuristic: new model requests that hit the runtime add token generation work. Use token-per-request average: Breeze 120 tokens, Muse 240, Atlas 600. For a baseline GPU pool with 100k qps tokens capacity per hour, adding combined burst of 10k requests/hour (mixed) increases token load by ~ (0.4*120 + 0.4*240 + 0.2*600)*10k = ~ (48+96+120)*10k = 2.64M tokens => represent ~2.64% of capacity (rough estimate).
region_breakdown: Primary regions considered: us-west1, us-east4, eu-central1, ap-southeast1.
Affinity % split (assumed): us-west1 35%, us-east4 30%, eu-central1 25%, ap-southeast1 10% for the customers targeted by these models.
Example projection table (peak KV GB by region, Scenario A week 2): us-west1: 18.2GB, us-east4: 15.6GB, eu-central1: 12.1GB, ap-southeast1: 4.8GB (includes replication buffer 10%).
mitigations_and_sensitivity: Shorten TTLs for ephemeral prefixes from 1h -> 15m reduces transient KV footprint by ~60% for short-lived sessions but increases miss rate — recommend pilot in single region first.
Regional pinning (force model x to region y for first 7 days) reduces cross-region cache duplication but increases latency for some users — trade-off quantified per region in the attached table.
Serve smaller quantized variants (Breeze-int4) as default for lower-tier traffic reduces KV size by ~35% and halves GPU token cost for short prompts; model-quality gating required.
Run a targeted seeded-warmup for top 5% hot prefixes to keep latency low while allowing TTL aggressive eviction for the tail.
If Atlas adoption grows beyond 50k active prefixes per region, require explicit pre-reservation of additional Redis shards + GPU warm capacity (see action items).
operational_recommendations: Capacity buffers: maintain 20% GPU headroom in primary regions for Scenario B style bursts; reduce to 12% if run staggered onboarding with regional pinning.
KV sizing: pre-provision cache clusters with 25% comfortable headroom over peak projected KV (account for replication and compaction variance).
Monitoring: add per-model per-region TTL hit/miss dashboards and a 'KV growth delta' alert (threshold 10GB/day) that triggers rollback gating for rollouts.
Release gating: require infra sign-off if projected region-level persistent KV > 50GB or GPU uplift > 18% compared to baseline.
Cost optimization: evaluate using a two-tier backend (local in-region Redis + cold long-term store) to push tail entries to cheaper storage after 3h.

SRE: add 'model-kv-footprint' timeseries to infra ingestion (Miguel) and backfill 30 days for baseline comparison.

open_questions: What is acceptable latency increase for 10% cost savings via quantized variants? Product to define SLO trade-off.
Is cross-region replication of KV required for regulatory data residency customers? If yes, we need to double-count KV in those regions.
Confirm target sample size for seeded-warmup experiment and how we'll collect effectiveness metrics (hit-rate improvements).
notes: This is a working doc — numbers are high-level estimates and should be used for planning, not committed billing.
If we proceed with Burst onboarding (Scenario B), plan an ops on-call window during the first 48 hours after global rollout.
